title: Signal · Friday 27 November
overview: The Bank of England eases UK bank capital rules while warning on AI financing, euro countries pick Pablo Hernández de Cos to lead the ECB, and SAP weighs at least 10,000 AI-driven job cuts.

top.headline: Bank of England eases UK bank capital rules as it warns on AI financing
top.summary: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee said on 26 November it has completed its review of bank capital. The PRA will consult on lower requirements tied to domestic lending, and with earlier changes Tier 1 requirements for major UK banks will fall by around 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets in normal times. The countercyclical buffer stays at 2 percent.
top.background: The same Financial Stability Report calls AI financing “increasingly complex, circular and opaque”, with hyperscalers on course to issue more than USD 305 billion of bonds in 2026.
top.why: London is easing for its banks while Bern debates more capital for UBS, a comparison the Swiss debate will pick up. The committee also lists AI agents, open-weight models and single-provider cloud outages as rising operational risks for banks.
top.watch_next: The PRA consultation on the domestic lending requirements.

top.headline: Euro countries pick Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
top.summary: Euro area member states agreed on 26 November to recommend Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next ECB president, with Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier for the Executive Board, EU Council President António Costa said, according to Reuters. Costa said this paves the way for the formal appointment in December.
top.background: Christine Lagarde leaves on 7 February 2027, almost nine months before her term ends, according to SRF. Hernández de Cos, 55, heads the BIS today, and the Netherlands withdrew its candidate, Klaas Knot.
top.why: The president shapes euro area rates for eight years, and SRF describes him as leaning towards lower rates, which bears on the franc and on the SNB. SRF also reports that Brunnermeier is set to become chief economist, the seat that prepares rate decisions.
top.watch_next: Opinions from the European Parliament and the ECB Governing Council before leaders make the appointment in December.

top.headline: SAP weighs at least 10,000 job cuts in an AI restructuring, Bloomberg reports
top.summary: SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs in an AI-driven restructuring, Bloomberg News reported on 26 November, according to Reuters. That would be at least 9 percent of its global workforce, and Bloomberg said the total could change after labour negotiations.
top.background: SAP, which Reuters calls Europe's most valuable tech company, declined to comment, and Reuters said it could not independently verify the report.
top.why: If confirmed, at least 9 percent of the jobs at Europe's most valuable tech company would go in a restructuring framed around AI, a reference point for bank boards setting their own AI cost targets. Banks that run finance and procurement on SAP will want to know what it means for support.
top.watch_next: Whether SAP confirms the plan and its timing.

items.headline: First Swiss-domiciled bitcoin ETF lists on SIX, with coins held by AMINA Bank
items.summary: SIX listed the Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT) on 26 November, with Pernet von Ballmoos as issuer and BIT Asset Management as sponsor and asset manager. FINMA approved the fund on 20 October. It holds bitcoin directly, without derivatives or lending, and AMINA Bank keeps the coins offline in Switzerland.
items.why: Private banks can now offer bitcoin as a Swiss fund in an ordinary securities account, which may sit more easily in mandates than exchange-traded notes.

items.headline: FCA says reports of AI-linked investment fraud rose nearly 400 percent in a year
items.summary: Reports of investment fraud mentioning suspected AI rose from 193 in 2024/25 to 956 in 2025/26, the FCA said on 26 November. A third of UK adults believe they saw an AI-made investment promotion in the past year, and only 49 percent think they could spot a faked video or voice of a well-known person.
items.why: Deepfake endorsements have become a volume problem, which strengthens the case for banks to flag payments to unauthorised firms before clients send money.

items.headline: Banks' agentic AI threatens Indian IT vendors' base revenue, Kotak report says
items.summary: Agentic AI at global banks could deflate the base business of Indian IT services firms, Kotak Institutional Equities said in a report carried by ANI on 26 November. It cites productivity gains of 20 to 40 percent in software development at some financial firms, and says AI could reduce incremental headcount needs in customer service and KYC.
items.why: Banks renegotiating outsourcing contracts have fresh grounds to ask vendors to pass on AI productivity in price.

items.headline: Glarner Kantonalbank sets 2030 targets under its new MOVE30 strategy
items.summary: Glarner Kantonalbank's MOVE30 strategy runs from 2027 to 2030 and targets a total capital ratio of at least 17 percent, a cost-income ratio of no more than 60 percent and a pre-tax return on equity of at least 7 percent, according to finews. The bank plans simpler processes and targeted use of AI.
items.why: A small cantonal bank now ties AI to a cost-income target, which usually turns into process redesign and tooling budgets once the strategy period starts in January.

items.headline: Lombard Odier sees low recession risk and AI as a key growth driver
items.summary: Samy Chaar, chief economist and CIO Switzerland at Lombard Odier, said on 26 November that recession risks are low and the cycle is not over, according to finews. The bank estimates that about 25 percent of companies use AI applications, a share that could rise to about 80 percent, and sees oil possibly well below USD 100 a barrel in 2027.
items.why: One of Geneva's largest private banks is positioning clients for a capital-heavy AI cycle on the day the Bank of England warned about how that cycle is financed.

items.headline: Geneva wealth manager NFG Partners opens a DFSA-regulated company in Dubai
items.summary: NFG Partners has set up NFG Partners (DIFC) Limited, regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority, to serve families, family offices, companies and institutional clients from the region, finews reported on 26 November. Founding partner John Barrowman leads the Dubai company.
items.why: Another Geneva firm follows Gulf families onshore, where clients typically keep several banking relationships across jurisdictions.

items.headline: Irish court refuses to sanction BAWAG's EUR 1.62 billion takeover of Permanent TSB
items.summary: Ireland's High Court refused on 26 November to sanction BAWAG's proposed EUR 1.62 billion acquisition of Permanent TSB, because minority shareholders did not vote separately from the government, which holds 57.5 percent, according to Reuters. The judgment says 64 percent of the other shareholders backed the scheme, short of the 75 percent required.
items.why: A procedural ruling can still stop a cross-border bank deal, a risk for any European consolidation that leans on a state shareholder's support.

items.headline: GTCR seeks equity partners for a USD 50 billion buyout of Global Payments
items.summary: GTCR is in talks with Blackstone, Apollo and Warburg Pincus about equity or preferred equity to help fund its planned buyout of Global Payments, valued at about USD 50 billion, according to Reuters, as reported by Fintech News Switzerland on 26 November. GTCR is the largest shareholder, with 16.35 percent, and no agreement has been reached.
items.why: Card processing for banks and merchants is moving towards private equity ownership, and the funding talks show how hard a deal of this size is to finance.

items.headline: Nvidia pauses server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, WSJ reports
items.summary: Nvidia told partners including Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks that regional partners meet US export rules, according to The Wall Street Journal, as reported by TechCrunch on 26 November. Chinese companies had been reaching Nvidia chips remotely through data centres there.
items.why: Banks and cloud buyers in Southeast Asia may wait longer for AI capacity, and export controls now reach where compute is hosted.

items.headline: Update: Microsoft declares a Code Red to restore services within an hour
items.summary: Microsoft has launched an internal Code Red after the Microsoft 365 outage of 12 and 13 November and aims to restore its services worldwide in under one hour, according to Reuters, as reported by ICTjournal on 26 November. A memo from Jason Henderson, president of M365 Core, calls it the largest incident in Exchange Online's history by customer impact.
items.why: Banks that run email and collaboration on Microsoft 365 can ask for the five workstreams, including regional isolation of traffic, in their next resilience review.

items.headline: FCC lets SpaceX put up to one million AI data-centre satellites in orbit
items.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX's Starmind project for up to one million satellites to serve as AI data centres, according to Inside IT on 26 November. The licence runs to November 2040, and the first data-centre satellite must be operating by November 2033.
items.why: Orbital compute remains a long-term bet with hard engineering hurdles, and the licence sets dated milestones that investors can track.

say_it_today: The Bank of England is cutting what it asks of UK banks by around 50 basis points while calling AI financing complex, circular and opaque. Switzerland is going the other way with UBS, and that contrast is likely to come up in any conversation about Swiss competitiveness.
